newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks end lower, spooked by profit warnings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks end lower, spooked by profit warnings.

text.p: U.S. blue chips stocks ended lower on Wednesday after two key computer companies warned of disappointing quarterly earnings, raising concerns that trouble might lie ahead for the technology sector.

The Dow Jones industrial average closed lower for the third straight session, down 42 points unofficially to 7718. The average slumped over sixty points soon after the opening of trading and remained in negative territory for the rest of the session.
The Wednesday morning sell-off was sparked after profit warnings by Gateway 2000 Inc and Seagate Technology Inc, analysts said.

Seagate, the leading U.S. disk drive-maker, after the market close Tuesday issued its second earnings warning in two weeks, blaming lackluster demand for its high-end products. Shares fell more than ten percent, down 5-1/4 to 36-1/4.

Gateway, a direct marketer of personal computers, said after the close it expected revenues for the second quarter to be about even with the first quarter's level of $1.42 billion. Its stock lost 2-5/8 to 32-1/8 on the New York Stock Exchange.
The bad news sparked concerns of earnings shortfalls in the technology sector, which has run up during the past month, and possibly the broader market.
"There's been some suspicion that if there's no inflation ahead, we might have a slowdown, which would hurt earnings generally," said Harry Laubscher, market analyst at Tucker Anthony.
Some analysts waved off the profit warnings, saying the sell-off was a "knee-jerk" reaction, noting that the weeks leading up to an earnings period are frequently peppered with earnings warnings.
"We are telling people to be very, very cautious. Start taking some profits and buy bonds for safety," he said.
Bonds rose, with the benchmark 30-year bond rising 13/32 to yield 6.69 percent.

Gary Loe of Anderson & Loe, a firm that advises money managers, said, "Some consolidation in stocks is certainly reasonable after the gains we've had. But my sense is we're in a very volatile period."
That volatility is expected to get stronger through the week as the "triple witching" expiration of options and futures on Friday nears.
Other techs suffered, including Intel Corp, Dell Computer Corp, Microsoft Corp and Compaq Computer Corp all closed lower.

Weighing on the Dow was IBM Corp, Philip Morris Cos Inc and Disney Corp, which lost 1-1/2 to 82-1/2 after Southern Baptists said they would boycott Disney and its subsidiaries, citing its "gay friendly" policies.

Tobacco stocks fell on fears a settlement between the industry, the public health community and state attorneys general would collapse. Philip Morris shed 1-1/4 to 45-1/2 on the Big Board. RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp also fell.
Some Dow stocks bucked the trend, depite the overall softness. American Express Co rose 1-3/8 to 77-3/4 as takeover rumors swirled.
Also stronger was Allied Signal Inc, which rose one to 83 after the aerospace company agreed to buy Grimes Aerospace, which makes aircraft lighting systems.
Boston Properties Inc rose seven percent, adding 1-3/4 to 26-3/4 in heavy trading after the $785 million initial public offering of the real estate investment trust headed by Mortimer Zuckerman.

Bucking the weak trend in technology, Jabil Circuit Inc jumped 13-3/8 to 82-1/4 after it posted strong third quarter earnings, set a two-for-one stock split and had its rating raised by Robertson Stephens to buy from market performer.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 42.07 to close officially at 7718.71.
Market breadth was negative. Decliners beat advancers 1294 to 1192 on volume of 491,683,870.
The S&P 500 index fell 5.32 to 889.10.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 10.68 points to 1432.43.
((-- Wall Street desk, 212-859-1881))
